sections.label: From two pizzas to two people

bullets.text: AI compresses research, testing, and initial building into work the author argues two people can undertake.
Qubit Teams couple imagining and building rather than simply shrinking the old team.
Vision frames possibilities; Reality builds durable systems, with leadership shifting as experiments mature.
AI absorbs iterative work so human effort concentrates on direction, taste, and strategic judgment.
AI enables many small bets; the scarce skill becomes recognizing signal and killing weak ideas.
Promising prototypes still face production pressures that make Reality's contribution indispensable.
Reality builds reusable foundations while Vision experiments, reducing the cost of each subsequent test.
Embedded guardrails and continuous verification are meant to preserve speed without abandoning quality.
A breakthrough shifts Vision toward focused execution and Reality toward product architecture in the same hour.
Shared system context, rather than handoff meetings, is supposed to carry that transition.

sections.label: A proposed stack for machine-speed work

bullets.text: The proposed stack combines continuous testing agents, shared organizational context, and pipelines that anticipate drift.
Human judgment governs what to amplify, discard, and override as more maintenance becomes automated.
The organizational bet is a network of experimental and supporting pairs, not just a smaller headcount.
As coordination recedes, the closing makes precise decisions and enduring responsibility the pair's central test.

notes.text: The two names can look like job titles, but the text calls them oscillating states. That distinction matters: the proposal depends on continuous mutual influence, not a miniature version of the old relay.
What evidence would be strong enough to move a bet from breadth to depth? The model makes experiments cheaper, but the passage still leaves the threshold for a real signal to human judgment.

The claim that code can be born compliant makes the surrounding environment do much of the quality work. What would continuous verification need to show before a pair could trust those guardrails over line-by-line review?

The organizational proposal spends AI's efficiency gains on more discovery rather than treating smaller teams as the endpoint. How would a company decide which pairs to stop and which deserve sustained backing?
